summary: A judge lifted the competency stay in a Fairbanks first-degree murder case indicted in January, allowing it to proceed after two earlier orders had halted it. A Fairbanks man arrested on Sunday was charged on Monday with first-degree burglary in a dwelling, a Class B felony, and with violating a domestic violence protective order. A ninth Fairbanks case number has stopped returning records in the state court's public database, and this one carried three filed domestic violence counts; the court's dispositions report, which refreshed on Oct. 5, records the other eight as closed cases. Three Fairbanks cases closed on Oct. 2 with two guilty pleas and a dismissal. The filing counts below are the weekly report's own counts for the week ending Oct. 5.

entries.title: Judge lifts competency stay in Fairbanks first-degree murder case
body: A judge has lifted the stay in a Fairbanks first-degree murder case that had been halted twice on questions of the defendant's competency to stand trial. Alaska CourtView records that a competency hearing was held on Monday, Oct. 5 at 2:30 p.m. in Courtroom 402 before Judge Brent Bennett, and gives the result as "Order on Competence. Stay Lifted."

The case is 4FA-26-00112CR, State of Alaska vs. Davenport, Brian Jeffery. It carries one count of murder in the first degree, intent to cause death, AS 11.41.100(a)(1)(A), an unclassified felony, offence-dated Jan. 20, 2026 at Fairbanks and recorded as domestic violence related. A grand jury indicted on the count on Jan. 29, 2026. He is charged, not convicted.

The court record shows the case was stayed on competency grounds twice before, by orders entered in April and in July, and that two confidential competency evaluations were filed, on July 7 and on Oct. 1. A competency hearing on Oct. 2 was continued to Monday. A docket entry dated Oct. 5 records findings and an order on competence for criminal proceedings, commitment and transport.
The contents of the order are not public and the court's event list shows no new trial date. Nothing in the court record describes the offence.

entries.title: Fairbanks man charged with first-degree burglary and violating a protective order
body: A criminal case was filed at Fairbanks on Monday, Oct. 5 over an arrest made the previous morning. Alaska CourtView records 4FA-26-02022CR, State of Alaska vs. Wright, Vincent F, with a status of Open.

The file carries two counts, both offence-dated Oct. 4 at Fairbanks: violating a domestic violence protective order, AS 11.56.740(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour recorded as domestic violence related; and burglary in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.300(a)(1), a Class B felony. No grand jury has heard the case; it proceeds on a complaint. He is charged, not convicted.

An arraignment was held on Oct. 5 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 102, with counsel appointed from the bench and conditions of release entered. The Public Defender Agency is attorney of record. Preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 15 and Oct. 22. The case judge is Peterson.

The Alaska State Troopers dispatch for Oct. 4 records that troopers were dispatched at 8:53 a.m. to a report of a man violating a domestic violence protective order, that they determined he committed the crimes of violating a protective order and burglary in the first degree, and that he was arrested and remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Facility. The trooper entry cited the burglary statute without a subsection; the charging document specifies burglary in a dwelling, which is the felony-class version of the offence.
Nothing in the record identifies any person recorded as a victim.

entries.title: A ninth Fairbanks case number stops returning records, and this one carried filed charges
body: A ninth Fairbanks criminal case number that appears in Alaska Court System records now returns No Records Found in Alaska CourtView, the court's public case lookup. 4FA-26-02006CR was searched twice by case number on the morning of Oct. 6 and returned no records both times, and a name search limited to cases filed since Sep. 1 also returned none.

The case was read in CourtView on Oct. 3. It was filed at Fairbanks on Oct. 2 and carried three counts, all offence-dated Aug. 7 at Fairbanks and all recorded as domestic violence related: assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, and two counts of assault when a child is present, all three Class A misdemeanours. Unlike the eight numbers already recorded, this one carried charges that had been filed rather than a count recorded as charging document pending.

The court's criminal dispositions report, which records cases that have closed, refreshed on Oct. 5 with a window running to that date. It records the other eight numbers as closed cases, with closing dates: 4FA-26-01862CR on Sep. 24, 4FA-26-01933CR and 4FA-26-01934CR on Sep. 26, 4FA-26-01904CR on Sep. 30, 4FA-26-01984CR on Oct. 1, 4FA-26-02004CR and 4FA-26-02013CR on Oct. 3 and 4FA-26-02018CR on Oct. 4. Seven of the eight carry a single count recorded as charging document pending or not filed, and no disposition code is printed against any of them.
The ninth number does not appear in that report. No explanation for any of the nine is offered here.

entries.title: Three Fairbanks cases closed on Oct. 2: two guilty pleas and a dismissal
body: The Alaska Court System's criminal dispositions report, which refreshed on Oct. 5 with a window running from Sep. 1 to Oct. 5, records three Fairbanks cases closed on Oct. 2.
4FA-25-01188CR, State of Alaska vs. Monge, Andrew Robert: one count of reckless driving, AS 28.35.400, offence-dated June 18, 2025, recorded as a guilty conviction after a guilty plea.

4FA-26-00973CR, State of Alaska vs. Sweetsir, Tessa Nicole: one count of criminal mischief in the fourth degree, property damage of $250 to $749, offence-dated May 17, 2026, recorded as a guilty conviction after a guilty plea.

4FA-26-01486CR, State of Alaska vs. Tucker, Bryan Edward: one count of criminal mischief in the fifth degree, damage under $250, offence-dated Aug. 2, 2026, dismissed under a plea agreement in another case.
The report records the outcome of each case and no sentence details. No announcement of any of the three was made by the Alaska Department of Law.

entries.title: A second fugitive-from-justice case is filed at Fairbanks
body: A second fugitive-from-justice case has been filed at Fairbanks. Alaska CourtView records 4FA-26-02023CR, State of Alaska vs. Defoyd, Lisa Lynnette, filed Oct. 5 with a status of Open.

The file carries one count of arrest prior to requisition, fugitive from justice, AS 12.70.120, offence-dated Oct. 4. No degree of offence is recorded, no offence location is printed and no requesting state is named. Under that statute none of those need appear until another state's requisition arrives.

An arraignment was held on Oct. 5 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 102, with conditions of release entered and bail recorded at $1,000. A fugitive from justice hearing is set for Nov. 4 at 1:30 p.m. The case judge is not yet assigned.
The other fugitive-from-justice case on this record, 4FA-26-01857CR, has had no docket entry since Sep. 19 and has a hearing set for Oct. 15.

entries.title: A case filed on Oct. 2 appears in the court database for the first time
body: A Fairbanks criminal case with a court file date of Friday, Oct. 2 appeared in Alaska CourtView for the first time on Oct. 6. The same number returned No Records Found when searched on the morning of Oct. 5.

The case is 4FA-26-02021CR, State of Alaska vs. Ewen, Daniel Edward, status Open. It carries three counts, all offence-dated Aug. 9 at Fairbanks: two counts of violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, AS 11.56.757(a)(misdB), Class B misdemeanours; and unlawful contact per court order, AS 11.56.750(a)(1)(A), a Class A misdemeanour recorded as domestic violence related. He is charged, not convicted.

The docket records the charging document and a summons requested on Oct. 2 and a summons issued on Oct. 5. No hearing is calendared and no attorney is entered for the defendant. The case judge is Bahr.

The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report lists the case under Friday, Oct. 2. The two previous weekly reports, run on the evenings of Oct. 3 and Oct. 4, did not contain it. Filing-day counts taken from that report are the counts at the time the report was run.

entries.title: Three Fairbanks-area cases opened without charges now carry them
body: Three criminal case numbers issued at Fairbanks on Oct. 4, each of which recorded one count as charging document pending or not filed, now carry filed charges.

4FA-26-02015CR, State of Alaska vs. Tritt, Michael: criminal trespass in the second degree, upon premises, AS 11.46.330(a)(1), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 3 at Fairbanks. The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records an arrest on the same charge at the 1000 block of Lacey Street at 7:23 p.m. on Oct. 3.

4FA-26-02016CR, State of Alaska vs. Baldwin, Thomas Joel: driving under the influence, breath alcohol .08 or over, AS 28.35.030(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 3 at Fairbanks. The trooper dispatch records a report of an impaired driver near Chena Pump at about 8:35 p.m. on Oct. 3.

4FA-26-02017CR, State of Alaska vs. Riva, Sarah: driving under the influence, AS 28.35.030(a), a Class A misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 3 at North Pole. This case appears in no police or trooper feed; the court file is the only public record of it. North Pole has no public incident feed.

All three are arraigned on Oct. 9 at 8:30 a.m. in Courtroom 102, and all three are charged, not convicted. Two further case numbers issued on Oct. 2 and Oct. 3, 4FA-26-02008CR and 4FA-26-02009CR, still record one count as charging document pending or not filed.

entries.title: Troopers record a death at a Fairbanks home
body: Alaska State Troopers responded with Steese EMS to Constitution Drive, Fairbanks, at about 12:40 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 5, for a medical assist. The dispatch states a person had collapsed and was unresponsive at home, that emergency intervention was unable to resuscitate them, and that they were pronounced dead at 1:14 a.m.
The dispatch records that nothing suspicious was noted and that the incident is considered closed. No name is published in the entry. The entry was posted at 1:51 a.m. on Oct. 6.

entries.title: Troopers forward charges over a reported conditions-of-release violation at North Pole
body: The Alaska State Troopers dispatch records that at 9:40 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 5 troopers responded to a report that Jess Eakin, 40, of North Pole was violating his conditions of release. The dispatch states that the investigation determined he committed the offences of violating conditions of release and unlawful contact in the first degree, and that charges were forwarded to the District Attorney's Office for review. The entry was posted at 6:18 p.m.

No arrest is recorded in the entry. No criminal court file exists: a search of Alaska CourtView under that name for cases filed since Sep. 1 returns no records. The offences above are as recorded by police, and no charge class is stated here, because none is on any court file.

A case number issued at Fairbanks under the same name on Oct. 4, 4FA-26-02018CR, was closed the same day with no charging document filed and has returned no records in the court's public database since Oct. 5.

entries.title: Second wanton waste case in a week filed at Delta Junction
body: A criminal case was filed at the Delta Junction court on Oct. 5 over an alleged hunting offence last month. Alaska CourtView records 4DJ-26-00061CR, State of Alaska vs. Guisasola, Kaleb Christopher, status Open.

The file carries two counts, both offence-dated Sep. 6 at Delta Junction: wanton waste of big game and wild fowl, AS 16.30.010(a), a Class A misdemeanour; and a non-criminal violation of a state regulation requiring that antlers or horns not be transported until all edible meat has been salvaged.

An arraignment is set for Oct. 6 at 3:00 p.m. at the Delta Junction Courthouse. The case judge is Young. He is charged, not convicted. A separate wanton waste case, 4DJ-26-00059CR, was filed at the same court on Sep. 30; the records do not connect the two.

entries.title: Fairbanks police record a disorderly conduct arrest on Dunkel Street
body: The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records an arrest at the 100 block of Dunkel Street at 1:37 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 5, on a charge recorded by police as disorderly conduct, creating a hazardous condition, a misdemeanour. The case number is 26003054 and the reporting officer is listed as Butler.

No criminal court file recording that charge appears in the Alaska Court System's weekly charges report for the week ending Oct. 5, and no charge class is stated here. The person named is arrested, not convicted.
